title: Adaptive Decision Lab for Safe Optimize Suggestion Activation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Optimize suggests batching and KV caching configs that can materially change per-token cost and latency. Past manual rollouts are slow and error-prone; naive auto-apply risks quality regressions or SLA violations. Goal: build an "Adaptive Decision Lab" — a safe autopilot that evaluates, stages, and (optionally) auto-activates optimize suggestions using risk scoring, synthetic canaries, operator-in-loop approvals, and deterministic rollback heuristics.

Scope: PoC supports three suggestion classes: batching_window_ms, kv_cache_ttl_seconds, and per_route_batch_threshold. The system evaluates suggestions against a telemetry contract, runs synthetic-twin canaries (simulated traffic + small real cohorts), computes a composite risk score (cost delta, latency delta, quality regression estimate), and executes one of: auto-apply, request-approval, or schedule-manual-adoption.

Success metrics (must be measurable):
- No noisy customer-impact incidents caused by auto-applied suggestions for 30 days in pilot.
- For applied suggestions: median cost per 1k tokens decreases >= 7% with P95 latency change <= +10% and quality regression <= 0.5% on eval prompts.
- Operator override rate <= 20% for suggestions marked auto-apply.

High-level design:
1) Ingest suggestion -> enrich with historical traffic profile (seq length distribution, routes, percentiles).
2) Synthesize a "twin" traffic generator using replay and randomized permutations to run candidate configs in a safe sandbox runtime.
3) Compute telemetery contract checks and risk score (weighted sum of cost_saving_score, latency_risk_score, quality_uncertainty_score).
4) Policy engine decides path: AUTO_APPLY | REQUIRES_APPROVAL | SCHEDULE_CANARY.
5) If canary: orchestrate small cohort in production (0.5-3% traffic) with fast-fail heuristics and a chill-window; if failure, automated revert + annotated incident.
6) Operator approval flow: expose preflight artifacts (sim logs, simulated metrics, diffs, PR to infra) in Console and Slack approval action.
7) Post-activation monitoring and automated rollback if contract breached.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow from suggestion detection to either auto-apply or canary activation works in staging with synthetic twin (demoable).
- Risk scoring engine exposes feature flags and tunables (weights, thresholds) and is covered by unit/integration tests.
- Canary orchestration supports timebox (chill window), traffic percentage ramps, and automatic rollback if any of: latency P95 increases beyond threshold, error rate increases by > 2x baseline, or quality metric drift > 0.5%.
- Console shows preflight report with cost delta, latency projections, and a one-click request-approval link.
- Playbook documented in runbook with steps for operator override, emergency rollback, and postmortem templates.
- PR created for sandbox runtime changes and gating policy code: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize-auto/pull/671

Out of scope for PoC: integration with Dedicated autoscaler policies, RBAC review for enterprise tenants, and model-card driven quality checks (future work).
